title: Ore. among top 3 states with highest odds of seeing Bigfoot
excerpt: Bigfoot gained national attention back in the 1960s thanks to that footage.
content:
Are you the type of person who believes the truth is out there?

Then perhaps you'd like to visit a state where the odds of catching a glimpse of Bigfoot are purportedly high?

Canada Sports Betting took the time to research these odds, and recently published a report based on the analysis of data points like the area's forest coverage and Bigfoot reports per 100,000 people.

When all was said and done, the top three states with the highest odds of seeing Bigfoot were found to be:

  1. Washington

  2. West Virginia

  3. Oregon

The odds of seeing Sasquatch in Washington state are 4.61 percent, the report claims, with 9.17 sightings per 100,000 people. Indeed, the Bigfoot Field Researchers Organization (BFRO) lists 734 reported sightings total of the mystery cryptid for the state, the highest out of the entire 50.

The last reported sighting on BFRO occurred in Skamania County back in May. During the daytime, too, no less.

"I was driving in the Gifford Pinchot National Forest on Wind River Road — approximately one to two miles south of Hemlock Road (north of Carson)," the report reads. "I noticed debris falling from the bank of the road and a large bolder in the ditch.

"I looked up the embankment to see what may have caused it. I was traveling about 50 MPH so the viewing was very brief. I saw a reddish brown furry figure standing at the edge of the embankment. The terrain behind it was heavy forestation. Because I was driving, it is hard to say the height and I did not see a face. It may have had its back to me but it was standing upright and definitely not human or a bear."

Bigfoot sightings have persisted throughout the United States since the legend first garnered widespread attention in the 1960s. Different states even have their own version of Mr. Foot: Florida has the skunk ape, for one, while Pennsylvania has the Albatwitch.

If you ever spot wildlife you don't recognize — or even wildlife you do — it is not recommended that you approach it.
